sources.title: Virginia Tech Dendrology — Norway spruce identification sheet
sources.scope: Selected actual institutional fact-sheet text accessed through web retrieval: pointed four-angled needles on woody sterigmata, slender orange-brown shoots and long thin-scaled mature cones. The model has partial insertion cues, not complete measured sterigmata or scale-tooth microanatomy. No quantitative natural cone-opening mechanics are imported.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected official identification-sheet text through web retrieval

findings.shape: Original conical branching hierarchy with drooping fine shoots, individual single pointed needle surfaces with partial brown insertion cues, scaly bark pigmentation and selected elongated pendent seed cones.
findings.surface: Original dark-green single pointed quadrangular needle cues, partial brown basal insertion cues, muted scaly-bark pigment and thin woody cone-scale studies. Natural wax, stomata and optical response are not calibrated.
findings.movement: The same trunk, branches, leaves and cones remain present. Working sway is small authored external branch deflection with anchored roots; no wind, stiffness, damping or physiological solver. Full cone maturation/release is explicitly unavailable. Full germination and organ-by-organ seed-to-tree development remain unavailable; the adult crown is not resized into a false developmental sequence.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual institutional species description read for conical habit and increasingly pendulous secondary branches with age. Cultivar extremes, horticultural size/rate figures and hardiness data are not generalized as measured model anatomy or native occurrence evidence. Selected actual institutional fact-sheet text accessed through web retrieval: pointed four-angled needles on woody sterigmata, slender orange-brown shoots and long thin-scaled mature cones. The model has partial insertion cues, not complete measured sterigmata or scale-tooth microanatomy. No quantitative natural cone-opening mechanics are imported.
corrections: Replaced sparse generic tiers with a conical branched crown and drooping secondary/fine shoots.
Added individual single quadrangular pointed needle surfaces rather than paired pine needles.
Increased foliage and added a terminal shoot after the initial crown looked sparse; raised low branch supports clear of the display ground.
Added elongated pendent cone studies and separated unavailable full reproductive release from working branch articulation.
Added retained-branch camera bounds and outward anatomy focus.
findings.residual: The conical crown and branch hierarchy remain too regular in places. Some lower diagnostic views obscure the cone behind retained shoots; sterigmata, scale margins, needle epidermis and natural optics are incomplete. No measured wind mechanics, age-specific allometry, full seed development or cone-release sequence.
